Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Grand Junction CO
1039 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- 2-4 more inches of snow possible throughout tonight and 
  Saturday morning in the San Juans, central Colorado mountains,
  and some mountain valleys.

- Temperatures will trend downward for the weekend, with most 
  desert valleys seeing their first freezing temperatures of the
  season.

- Active weather is possible through much of Thanksgiving week.
  Stay tuned for updates to timing and impacts as they become
  available.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 846 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

SNOW TO CONTINUE THROUGH SATURDAY MORNING:

Low pressure is situated over the Great Basin tonight, and as a
result, modest moisture continues to flow into our region amid 
the southwesterly flow. This has and will continue to support 
scattered showers tonight and through the majority of Saturday 
morning. The trough axis swings through near mid-day tomorrow, 
quickly shutting off the tap of moisture and ending the majority
of active weather in our CWA. Until then, look for another one 
to three tenths of liquid precipitation to fall across the San 
Juans, central Colorado mountains, and along US-50 (generally 
east of Montrose). Cooler temperatures will continue to support 
lower snow levels, and so with most remaining precipitation 
expected over mountains and mountain valleys, snow should 
dominate throughout the end of this event. Additional 
accumulations will generally be under 3 inches, though some 
locally higher amounts are possible on the northern slopes of 
the San Juans where snowfall is expected to be more persistent 
through the night. Otherwise, temperatures have notably dropped 
behind the frontal boundary which passed through today, which 
means overnight lows for the next several night are tracking to
drop below freezing for a large swath of the region. Any valley
locations which have yet to hit freezing temperatures should 
expect to drop below freezing as a result.

LIGHT SHOWERS EARLY NEXT WEEK:

A low-amplitude ridge builds in behind the exiting trough 
Saturday evening into Sunday morning. Skies may clear out some 
during the overnight period, which would support a localized fog
risk in some valleys, though the current forecast isn't overly 
bullish on widespread saturation at the surface. Chances for fog
are highest further north in the Uinta and Yampa Basins though.
By Sunday evening, upper-level flow will be turning back 
southwesterly ahead of another approaching trough. Moisture and 
upper-level support is unimpressive with this storm, so current 
expectations are for only light showers Sunday evening through 
Tuesday morning. Snow accumulations are on track to sit well 
below advisory level.

There is a vague signal of another system passing through in 
the latter half of next week, but cluster analysis shows a wide 
range of outcomes with low confidence on when wet weather would 
arrive, if at all. Though confidence is extremely low at this 
time, this potential storm could be impactful to Thanksgiving 
travel. Stay tuned over the coming days for additional updates 
regarding the late-week weather, especially if you are planning 
to travel for the holiday.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 1039 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

Snow showers continue to drift northeastward over the mountains
and adjacent valleys of western Colorado. This is leading to IFR
to MVFR flight conditions in lower clouds and rain or snow
showers. The system driving these showers will move through by
tomorrow morning with improving conditions expected at most TAF
sites by mid-day. Terrain obscuration over the higher mountains
may linger into the evening hours before the moisture is scoured
out.
